items.text: There's almost nothing harder than writing, if you’re out of the groove. It's hard to get into it, so then once you're into it, it’s so frustrating to be taken out of it. This is why writing and small kids mix so poorly.

items.author: David Senra
items.text:
.@brian_armstrong was a conflict-averse CEO until he reprogrammed his brain:

“I remember writing this down a lot. ‘I love conflict. I love conflict. I love conflict.”

“I was like, ‘I need to reprogram my brain to not think of this as super stressful.”

“It doesn’t mean I go out and actively seek conflict just to piss people off, but if it does happen, I can get somewhat excited about it now.”

items.author: John Asghar
items.text:
People need to learn the teachings of Mr. Miyagi….

Too many seriously undervalue repetition.

Every case is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned and refine your technique. There is tremendous skill and insight in repeating the same movement over and over and finding ways to improve it.

That is how expertise develops. Performing surgery safely while making it look routine and easy takes years of practice, knowledge and judgment.

quoted.author: Caffeinatedoc
quoted.text:
Unpopular opinion, but surgery is 99% repetition and 1% talent. And honestly, I’m being generous with that 1%

Medicine, on the other hand, requires actual grey matter. No amount of hands-on experience can compensate for what's missing upstairs.

items.author: Joe Hudson
items.text:
If you want to surf, you don’t ask the ocean to be different
You seek to understand how it moves.

If a plant wilts, you don’t tell it to “try harder.”
You seek to understand how it thrives.
